This is a very dubious article that is misrepresenting what is common in technology. For example, when you click on ANY internet content like a video, you will want to receive that content in the fastest way possible. If you are in New York, you DO NOT want to be pulling that video from servers in Tokyo, if the video is on a server right next to you. The same goes for literally all content on the web that is cached or served from multiple locations.

Each cell tower acts as its own "POP" (think of it as an access point like a router). Where that tower is located determines where it will get content from. So when your phone downloads ANY content from the Internet, the location of the tower it is connected to is necessary to get that content in the most efficient way possible.

So, in order for you to receive push notifications on your phone... it needs to know where you are, or it will not work. To call this "location tracking" is disingenuous albeit correct in the technical sense that it probably exists in some server log somewhere.

The bottom line is that there is NO way to use a mobile phone without someone knowing where that phone was. To act like they are using this as "backdoor spying" is fucking reatarded.
